domains.name: IT
domains.label: Poesis for IT
tags: First domain — foundations and planned workflows
domains.blurb: Planned IT definition, evidence review, appraisal and analysis workflows, over existing authentication, specification and engine foundations.

actorTypes.name: IT service owner
actorTypes.hook: Accept service commitments against dependencies and evidence.
actorTypes.body: Own service outcomes, agree operating boundaries, and coordinate affected owners during changes, incidents and recovery reviews.

actorTypes.name: Application owner
actorTypes.hook: Keep application responsibilities and service dependencies explicit.
actorTypes.body: Maintain application commitments and lifecycle decisions, identify consuming services, and transfer responsibility with accepted evidence.

actorTypes.name: IT risk owner
actorTypes.hook: Own the consequences of a bounded risk decision.
actorTypes.body: Assess exposure, propose compensating controls, and provide evidence for exception renewal or closure without assuming approval authority.

actorTypes.name: Exception approver
actorTypes.hook: Decide whether a scoped, time-bound exception is acceptable.
actorTypes.body: Review justification, authority, expiry and compensating-control evidence before granting, renewing or revoking an exception.

actorTypes.name: API product owner
actorTypes.hook: Evolve a shared interface with its consumers.
actorTypes.body: Review contract changes, identify affected consumers, and agree migration and deprecation conditions supported by compatibility evidence.

actorTypes.name: Operational knowledge owner
actorTypes.hook: Transfer decisions and unresolved obligations with the service.
actorTypes.body: Curate authoritative decisions, operating evidence and open questions so the receiving owner can explicitly accept a handover.

actorTypes.name: Vulnerability manager
actorTypes.hook: Prioritize vulnerabilities in the context of affected services.
actorTypes.body: Reconcile findings with deployed components, assess exposure and business criticality, and route remediation to accountable owners.

actorTypes.name: Product security engineer
actorTypes.hook: Demonstrate whether a mitigation addresses the relevant exposure.
actorTypes.body: Investigate applicability, propose fixes or compensating controls, and inspect verification evidence before closing a finding.

actorTypes.name: IT procurement manager
actorTypes.hook: Compare supplier commitments against the services that depend on them.
actorTypes.body: Review contractual changes, renewal conditions and exit obligations with service and risk owners before committing a purchase.

actorTypes.name: Third-party risk analyst
actorTypes.hook: Connect supplier evidence to the scope of actual dependence.
actorTypes.body: Assess assurance scope, evidence age, subcontractor dependencies and concentration exposure while preserving unresolved questions.

actorTypes.name: IT resilience manager
actorTypes.hook: Assess whether recovery evidence supports service commitments.
actorTypes.body: Review disruption scenarios and exercise results with service and business owners, and record gaps between targets and demonstrated recovery.

actorTypes.name: Disaster-recovery coordinator
actorTypes.hook: Coordinate recovery in a dependency-aware order.
actorTypes.body: Prepare exercise sequences, identify shared-resource conflicts, and collect timed recovery and data-restoration evidence for review.

actorTypes.name: Data owner
actorTypes.hook: Accept data commitments with producers and consumers.
actorTypes.body: Decide acceptable uses and quality expectations, resolve conflicting consumer requirements, and approve contract changes within authority.

actorTypes.name: Data steward
actorTypes.hook: Make data-quality evidence and contract differences inspectable.
actorTypes.body: Maintain definitions and lineage evidence, assess quality findings, and prepare changes for accountable owner and consumer review.

actorTypes.name: Incident commander
actorTypes.hook: Trace a software incident to affected business activities.
actorTypes.body: Coordinate response from observed disruption through deployed components and services to business processes and owners, distinguishing confirmed impact from possible exposure.

actorTypes.name: Business-process owner
actorTypes.hook: Make the business consequences of an IT disruption explicit.
actorTypes.body: Identify critical activities and service dependencies, confirm business disruption, agree workarounds, and set recovery priorities with incident and service owners.

actorTypes.name: CTO / CIO
actorTypes.hook: Evaluate a shared definition model for a bounded IT decision.
actorTypes.body: A pilot can compare reconciliation work, decision quality and governance costs. Integrated inventory, appraisal and generation remain planned; whole-estate savings are not assumed.

actorTypes.name: Enterprise Architect
actorTypes.hook: Trace definitions to accepted intent and inspected evidence.
actorTypes.body: Explore planned authoring, dependency analysis and artifact generation. Source revisions, deployed observations and simulation assumptions remain distinct evidence boundaries.

actorTypes.name: CISO / Security leadership
actorTypes.hook: Make a stated appraisal scope and its missing evidence visible.
actorTypes.body: Selected GDPR/NIS2 templates and quality vocabularies exist; binding, observations and appraisal are planned integrations. Measure coverage and reconstruction effort, not automatic legal compliance.

actorTypes.name: Platform / Ops / SRE lead
actorTypes.hook: Inspect the boundary between definitions and operations.
actorTypes.body: API and execution source can support a bounded integration experiment. Observation identity, effect authority, failure receipts and recovery must be accepted for the selected environment.

actorTypes.name: Head of AI
actorTypes.hook: Evaluate AI answers against authorized, attributable context.
actorTypes.body: Planned read-only context and copilot routes need citation, abstention and injection tests. Direct authoring is valid without sourcing; typed context alone does not make action safe.

actorTypes.name: Specification reader / modeler
actorTypes.hook: Compare a system description with a declared modeling contract.
actorTypes.body: Read source specifications and sourced vocabularies, inspect examples and record interpretation limits before choosing an implementation.

actorTypes.name: Research reviewer
actorTypes.hook: Distinguish a research hypothesis from an accepted requirement.
actorTypes.body: Compare explanations, inspect case evidence and follow decision records before proposing a specification change.

actorTypes.name: Authorized integration client
actorTypes.hook: Exchange identified definitions within an explicit access boundary.
actorTypes.body: A consuming service or tool requests pinned context, publishes reviewed drafts or consumes committed changes under its own authenticated identity.

actorTypes.name: Assessment runner
actorTypes.hook: Evaluate identified inputs and retain unknown results.
actorTypes.body: A scheduler or appraisal client supplies pinned rules and instances, requests pure verdicts and routes findings to an accountable reviewer.

actorTypes.name: Delivery agent
actorTypes.hook: Produce artifacts under declared grants and review boundaries.
actorTypes.body: A host-bound software agent receives a scoped task, resolves instructions and submits artifacts for checks and human review without assuming authority to deploy.

pains.pain: Collection scope, incomplete runs and stale evidence are mistaken for current coverage.
pains.cost: Reviews rely on uninspected or outdated inputs and repeat work when collection failures emerge late.

pains.pain: Access assignments drift from responsibilities and identity-provider changes.
pains.cost: Excess privileges persist while legitimate work is blocked by missing or stale assignments.

pains.pain: Reviewers work from different selections and lose related decisions across meeting notes.
pains.cost: Decisions cannot be compared or reconstructed against the same agenda, subject set and evidence boundaries.

pains.pain: A blocking finding identifies a problem without a clear route to correction and renewed review.
pains.cost: Rejected proposals and uncovered obligations remain unresolved while reviewers repeat the same checks.

pains.pain: Selected vocabulary and unbound templates are mistaken for complete, applicable obligations.
pains.cost: Subjects or concerns are omitted and requirements are applied without a justified adopting scope.

pains.pain: Incorrect bindings, unsupported narrative and partial files pass for completed deliverables.
pains.cost: Reviews discover missing evidence and output errors only after reports have been distributed.

pains.pain: Dependent definitions remain trusted after a foundation is invalidated.
pains.cost: Continued use relies on obsolete eligibility and bypasses the renewed review required by changed foundations.

pains.pain: Evidence is discarded too early or retained indefinitely without a justified preservation policy.
pains.cost: Historical decisions become unreviewable or unnecessary retained information creates avoidable exposure.

pains.pain: A rule revision changes established verdicts without an inspected explanation.
pains.cost: New false positives, missed violations and unknown outcomes alter decisions before their causes are understood.

pains.pain: Host or model selection changes behavior without verifying workload quality, instruction delivery or disclosure limits.
pains.cost: Required guidance and checks disappear or unsuitable model routes produce costly, untrustworthy work.

pains.pain: Individually valid parallel agent outputs overwrite or contradict accepted work.
pains.cost: Combined artifacts lose coherence and attribution despite each isolated output passing its checks.

pains.pain: Service commitments have no agreed map of dependencies and accountable owners.
pains.cost: Changes and ownership transfers leave obligations unassigned and affected services overlooked.

pains.pain: Temporary exceptions remain in force after their justification or controls expire.
pains.cost: Exposure accumulates without a current decision, a responsible risk owner or proof that compensating controls still work.

pains.pain: A shared API changes before all affected consumers and migration conditions are known.
pains.cost: Uncoordinated upgrades and deprecations disrupt dependent services and force emergency compatibility work.

pains.pain: Security findings are ranked without reliable deployed-service context or mitigation evidence.
pains.cost: Teams spend effort on the wrong exposure and close findings without establishing that affected services are protected.

pains.pain: Supplier assurances and exit promises are detached from the services that depend on them.
pains.cost: Procurement and renewal decisions accept obligations or transition risks that service owners cannot substantiate.

pains.pain: Recovery targets assume dependency sequences and restoration results that exercises have not demonstrated.
pains.cost: Services miss recovery commitments when shared resources, upstream dependencies or data restoration behave differently than assumed.

pains.pain: Data producers and consumers discover incompatible meanings or quality expectations only after a change.
pains.cost: Downstream decisions and integrations fail while teams reconstruct what each party believed the data contract guaranteed.

pains.pain: We know which software failed, but not which business processes are disrupted or whom to notify.
pains.cost: Response priorities follow technical alarms instead of confirmed business consequences, delaying workarounds and recovery for critical activities.

pains.pain: The architecture repository is out of date the day it’s written.
pains.cost: Hand-maintained models detach from the territory the moment delivery moves on — and every decision made on them inherits the drift.

pains.pain: Compliance is reconstructed in spreadsheets before every audit.
pains.cost: Posture exists only at audit time; between audits, nobody can answer what is actually covered.

pains.pain: Impact analysis is a guess made in a meeting.
pains.cost: Coupling is discovered in incident reviews, after the change shipped.

pains.pain: Every deliverable is hand-crafted, again and again.
pains.cost: ADR packs, evidence, baselines, and roadmaps are rebuilt by hand — and stale against each other by the time they ship.

pains.pain: Governance drifts from what actually runs.
pains.cost: The declared estate and the running estate diverge silently — until an audit or an incident exposes the gap.

pains.pain: AI agents act on stale wikis and tribal knowledge.
pains.cost: Without a trustworthy machine-readable source of truth, agent autonomy is either blocked or reckless.

pains.pain: Anything can change anything — there is no approval trail.
pains.cost: Definitions, standards, and obligations mutate without review; who approved what, and when, is unanswerable.

pains.pain: Every framework lives in its own silo — and they collide on your desk.
pains.cost: TOGAF, ISO, GDPR, and NIS2 each demand their own registry and their own reconciliation; overlaps and conflicts are discovered by accident.

pains.pain: Your governance model is trapped in a vendor’s proprietary format.
pains.cost: Obligations, architecture, and compliance mappings live in tool-specific silos — migrating tools means re-authoring your governance.

pains.pain: Architecture, compliance, and quality tools don’t speak to each other.
pains.cost: Each tool keeps its own model of the same IT reality; integrations are bespoke mappings that rot, and knowledge stays siloed per tool and per team.

pains.pain: AI agents ship work nobody scoped, gated, or can replay.
pains.cost: Agentic delivery state is trapped in chat sessions; pull requests appear without a mandate; there is no event log and no human authority at the layer where it matters.

pains.pain: A modeling decision cites an example as though it were an executed test.
pains.cost: A reviewer cannot distinguish a plausible explanation from evidence that rules out alternatives.

pains.pain: The reason for a decision stays in an email thread instead of reaching the next reviewer.
pains.cost: In a manual handoff, the next reviewer repeats interviews to recover assumptions and unresolved objections.

painGroups.lead: Purpose, rules, and constraints scattered across people, meetings, documents, and tools.
Every handoff reconstructed THINK — and lost a little of it each time.
THINK artifacts went stale as BUILD and RUN changed — definition and reality drifted apart.
Keep the speed: every artifact drifts further from intent, compounding at machine pace.
Restore alignment at every handoff: prompts, reviews, corrections, and controls consume the acceleration gain.
Human attention becomes the control plane — understanding, validation, coordination, and accountability remain scarce.

useCases.name: Configure repository collection boundaries
useCases.goal: Select repository branches, paths and revision boundaries so inspected evidence matches the intended acquisition scope.

useCases.name: Diagnose and recover incomplete collection
useCases.goal: Identify failed or partial acquisition runs, correct their causes and resume collection without presenting missing evidence as complete coverage.

useCases.name: Set and review evidence-refresh expectations
useCases.goal: Agree refresh expectations and inspect source age, failed refreshes and coverage limits before using collected evidence.

useCases.name: Review operation-specific privileges
useCases.goal: Review tenant, object and action permissions against assigned responsibilities and remove unnecessary authority.

useCases.name: Restore identity-provider synchronization
useCases.goal: Reconcile external identity and group changes with local access assignments, inspect synchronization failures and verify revoked access is no longer granted.

useCases.name: Prepare and conduct a multi-item governance session
useCases.goal: Prepare a related decision agenda, record participation and retain each revision-bound decision and condition without treating a meeting vote as authorization by itself.

useCases.name: Resolve a blocked change request
useCases.goal: Inspect blocking validation and lifecycle findings, correct the proposal and submit the revised scope for renewed review.

useCases.name: Retrieve the basis of a historical decision
useCases.goal: Retrieve the decided revision, recorded identity, supporting evidence and conditions relevant to a historical decision, retaining attribution gaps.

useCases.name: Define and reuse a scoped review lens
useCases.goal: Save explicit subject-selection and dependency-traversal rules and reuse them with visible snapshot boundaries across reviews.

useCases.name: Inspect one subject across framework perspectives
useCases.goal: Compare architecture, security and quality classifications of the same identified subject without confusing classification with obligation applicability.

useCases.name: Compose and reuse a governance selection
useCases.goal: Save a pinned selection of governance packages and reuse it while separately reviewing applicability for each adopting scope.

useCases.name: Resolve competing obligations before adoption
useCases.goal: Compare overlapping requirements, record interpretations and obtain an accountable resolution of incompatible obligations before adoption.

useCases.name: Identify gaps in selected vocabulary coverage
useCases.goal: Compare selected vocabulary against an explicit subject and concern inventory, exposing uncovered areas without claiming legal completeness.

useCases.name: Author and maintain reusable output bindings
useCases.goal: Define versioned template fields and source bindings that produce consistent named artifact families from pinned definitions.

useCases.name: Preview bindings before generating an artifact
useCases.goal: Inspect sample binding resolution and missing inputs before accepting a template for document generation.

useCases.name: Set grounding constraints for generated narrative
useCases.goal: Specify source requirements and editorial constraints for generated fields, then review citations and unsupported statements before accepting output.

useCases.name: Operate recurring report production
useCases.goal: Schedule version-pinned report production and detect failed or late runs before a review depends on the output.

useCases.name: Investigate partial or failed generation
useCases.goal: Inspect job completion, errors and partial outputs to decide what can be reused and what must be regenerated and reviewed.

useCases.name: Turn uncovered obligations into corrective proposals
useCases.goal: Turn scoped findings into owned definition-change proposals and verify resolution through a subsequent appraisal rather than merely closing a task.

useCases.name: Bind selected obligations to an organizational scope
useCases.goal: Establish the subjects, conditions and accountable interpretation that make selected obligations applicable to a specific adopting scope.

useCases.name: Assess dependent definitions after foundation invalidation
useCases.goal: Inspect dependent definition eligibility after a referenced foundation is invalidated and determine which continued uses require renewed review.

useCases.name: Agree evidence-preservation requirements
useCases.goal: Agree retention purpose, duration, access and disposal constraints for decision evidence, distinguishing agreed policy from demonstrated enforcement.

useCases.name: Qualify a rule revision against reference cases
useCases.goal: Compare old and proposed rule verdicts on pinned reference inputs, investigate changed or unknown results and record acceptance before adoption.

useCases.name: Agree a reusable domain typing contract
useCases.goal: Agree a versioned vocabulary and its constraints with adopters, using examples and counterexamples to expose incompatible interpretations.

useCases.name: Qualify transfer between independent processors
useCases.goal: Compare exported and imported definitions against an explicit conformance profile, including identity, lifecycle meaning and nonconformant draft preservation.

useCases.name: Approve an agent resource and action mandate
useCases.goal: Review resource/action grants against a bounded assignment and its expiry, then check those grants and the target baseline before mediated work. Mandate review is planned; grant checking alone is not authenticated human approval.

useCases.name: Qualify model routing for a workload
useCases.goal: Compare candidate model routes against workload-specific quality, cost and disclosure criteria using retained evaluation evidence.

useCases.name: Qualify instruction delivery on another host
useCases.goal: Verify that a target host receives the pinned instructions and declared checks, distinguishing delivery from model adherence before migration.

useCases.name: Reconcile conflicting parallel agent outputs
useCases.goal: Resolve overlapping edits against a shared baseline while retaining attribution and revalidating the combined artifacts before acceptance.

useCases.name: Assess application decommissioning prerequisites
useCases.goal: Identify dependent consumers, retained obligations and missing evidence before approving an application retirement boundary; execution remains a separate operation.

useCases.name: Accept a service responsibility baseline
useCases.goal: Agree service commitments, application dependencies and accountable owners against a dated evidence baseline.

useCases.name: Transfer service ownership
useCases.goal: Obtain explicit acceptance of service responsibilities, active exceptions and unresolved obligations by the receiving owner.

useCases.name: Review a time-bound risk exception
useCases.goal: Decide a scoped exception with explicit authority, expiry, risk ownership and compensating-control evidence.

useCases.name: Renew or close a risk exception
useCases.goal: Review current exposure and control evidence before renewing, revoking or closing an exception at its review boundary.

useCases.name: Review a breaking API contract change
useCases.goal: Identify affected consumers and inspect compatibility evidence before accepting an interface change and migration conditions.

useCases.name: Coordinate an API deprecation
useCases.goal: Agree consumer migration and retirement prerequisites while making unknown consumers and unresolved compatibility visible.

useCases.name: Hand over operational decisions and evidence
useCases.goal: Give a receiving service owner authoritative decisions, source evidence and unresolved questions sufficient to review and accept a handover.

useCases.name: Prioritize vulnerabilities by service exposure
useCases.goal: Relate findings to deployed components, affected services and business criticality to assign justified remediation priorities and owners.

useCases.name: Review vulnerability mitigation evidence
useCases.goal: Decide whether observed verification supports closure of a finding or requires a separately approved, time-bound exception.

useCases.name: Assess a supplier change against service commitments
useCases.goal: Review changed supplier terms and assurance evidence against dependent services, accountable owners and unresolved exposure.

useCases.name: Review supplier exit readiness
useCases.goal: Assess replacement dependencies, portability evidence and retained obligations before accepting a supplier exit plan.

useCases.name: Review a service recovery exercise
useCases.goal: Compare observed recovery time and data restoration with service and business commitments, retaining untested scenarios and evidence gaps.

useCases.name: Resolve recovery dependency conflicts
useCases.goal: Identify incompatible recovery sequences and shared-resource assumptions before agreeing a service recovery exercise plan.

useCases.name: Review a data contract change
useCases.goal: Review schema, meaning and quality changes with affected producers and consumers before accepting migration conditions.

useCases.name: Resolve competing data-quality requirements
useCases.goal: Agree scoped quality expectations and evidence requirements when consumers need different freshness, completeness or accuracy.

useCases.name: Trace a software incident to affected business processes
useCases.goal: Trace an observed software incident through identified deployed components and service dependencies to affected business processes and owners, distinguishing confirmed disruption, possible exposure and missing evidence to prioritize response.

useCases.name: Read and model a governance decision
useCases.goal: Interpret the primitive, typing, governance-grammar and lifecycle clauses relevant to a proposed decision, identifying permitted representations and constraints without claiming that a processor enforces them.

useCases.name: Describe a service contract and its attribution
useCases.goal: Select sourced HTTP, IT-domain and provenance concepts for a service description, checking the meaning and attribution of each assertion. Vocabulary does not implement the service or prove its behavior.

useCases.name: Describe payment request and notification boundaries
useCases.goal: Use sourced gRPC, GraphQL and WebSocket concepts to describe request, response and notification boundaries in a payment example. Application payment rules and delivery guarantees require separate definitions and evidence.

useCases.name: Describe payment settlement and recovery boundaries
useCases.goal: Use sourced JDBC, Kafka and AMQP concepts to describe transaction and messaging boundaries in a settlement example, exposing the recovery assumptions that vocabulary alone cannot establish.

useCases.name: Review sourced obligations before binding them
useCases.goal: Prepare a source-linked shortlist of architecture, quality and regulatory requirements for a bounded IT review.

useCases.name: Review a governance package upgrade
useCases.goal: Compare revised financial-resilience, delivery and service-management source content with the selected package versions and identify obligations needing renewed adopter review. A source update does not itself change accepted obligations.

useCases.name: Review a model research question
useCases.goal: Trace a non-normative modeling question to its explanations and recorded decision status.

useCases.name: Test and propose a grammar extension
useCases.goal: Turn a demonstrated modeling limit into a reviewable compatibility-aware Change Proposal.

useCases.name: Incorporate an accepted grammar extension
useCases.goal: Incorporate an approved grammar change with explicit compatibility and migration boundaries.

useCases.name: Author and approve a shared definition
useCases.goal: Replace a document-only change with an attributable, revision-bound definition decision.

useCases.name: Reconcile code evidence into reviewed definitions
useCases.goal: Turn competing source-revision candidates into attributable definition drafts for review.

useCases.name: Consume authorized definition context
useCases.goal: Give an integration client a policy-filtered, pinned context snapshot without granting authority to change systems.

useCases.name: React to a committed definition change
useCases.goal: Refresh a downstream view from committed changes without repeated full polling.

useCases.name: Review a scoped IT appraisal
useCases.goal: Review versioned findings with explicit applicability, input identity and missing evidence.

useCases.name: Review recurring patient-portal appraisal
useCases.goal: Compare successive portal appraisal results, review corrective proposals and decide what needs reappraisal. Operational conclusions require supplied deployment observations with explicit coverage and freshness; recurring scheduling is a separate prerequisite.

useCases.name: Inspect a change before committing to it
useCases.goal: Trace affected definitions and obligations, then record what remains unknown before deciding.

useCases.name: Ask an IT question and inspect its sources
useCases.goal: Obtain a read-only answer whose claims can be checked against authorized definition snapshots.

useCases.name: Generate and review an architecture decision pack
useCases.goal: Assemble an ADR pack and evidence summary from the same pinned inputs, then review the substantive result.

useCases.name: Execute a bounded response and inspect the receipt
useCases.goal: Perform a named authorized operation and retain enough evidence to decide whether recovery is needed.

useCases.name: Deliver a reviewed artifact through a local workflow
useCases.goal: Produce a scoped artifact through an attributable local method, checks and human review.

useCases.name: Set up a workspace and publish checked artifacts
useCases.goal: Reproduce a pinned local delivery environment and carry the same declared artifact checks into controlled CI publication.

useCases.name: Reuse captured delivery evidence as definition proposals
useCases.goal: Turn a pinned artifact and its captured journal into inspectable candidates without confusing generated work with deployed behavior.

useCases.name: Extract definition candidates from a code revision
useCases.goal: Analyze a pinned repository revision and inspect candidate subjects, relationships, provenance and uncertainty before any client promotes a draft. Inspected source is not evidence of deployed behavior.

useCases.name: Read and revise definitions through the API
useCases.goal: Create, query and revise typed definitions through the REST contract, inspecting validation, revision and access responses without treating a successful draft write as approval.

useCases.name: Qualify an execution adapter for an integration
useCases.goal: Check a selected adapter's transport, authority and failure contract against a named integration, distinguishing supported operations from planned adapter coverage.

useCases.name: Submit a contribution to a declared panel
useCases.goal: Post a candidate to a declared panel and inspect schema, identity, confidence-envelope and rejection responses under the client/server contract. Acceptance into collection is not definition approval.

useCases.name: Close a contribution collection for review
useCases.goal: Request sealing or abandonment of a contribution collection and inspect concurrent-intake outcomes and snapshot readiness. Closing collection does not approve or activate a definition.

useCases.name: Inspect retained contribution evidence
useCases.goal: Retrieve stored candidates and their captured evidence to inspect provenance and conflicting assertions, making missing audit, integrity or promoted-draft links explicit.

useCases.name: Resolve the next eligible workflow step
useCases.goal: Resolve eligible steps from workflow configuration and recorded outcomes on a supported adapter; leave dispatch to the host rather than treating resolution as execution.

useCases.name: Validate a mediated artifact write
useCases.goal: Check a proposed write set against a matched schema and inspect structured-data or Markdown-metadata violations before writing. Passing validation does not establish prose quality or acceptance.

useCases.name: Inspect a captured harness invocation sequence
useCases.goal: Read correlated session-journal records to reconstruct captured harness invocations and their outcomes, distinguishing absent records from evidence that no action occurred.

useCases.name: Assign a delivery responsibility from the role catalog
useCases.goal: Select portfolio, program, team and specialist roles for a delivery responsibility and make their boundaries explicit without treating a role definition as an authenticated authority grant.

useCases.name: Select a practice playbook for a delivery task
useCases.goal: Choose a domain or practice playbook for a named task and inspect its applicability and required evidence; reusable guidance does not prove agent adherence.

useCases.name: Define a delivery ceremony and its handoffs
useCases.goal: Specify the sequence of roles, context and artifacts for a ceremony, identifying human-decision checkpoints separately from the planned implementation that authenticates them.

useCases.name: Select versioned instructions for an engineering role
useCases.goal: Identify the versioned instructions governing a role's engineering work and distinguish advisory guidance from requirements enforced by separate executable gates.

useCases.name: Define a deliverable schema and template
useCases.goal: Select a schema and Markdown template for a named deliverable and inspect required metadata, content and references before using them as a write contract.

useCases.name: Install a pinned agentic workspace
useCases.goal: Set up a selected harness, organization and host combination while preserving existing work, checking version compatibility separately from the manual setup route.

useCases.name: Publish artifacts through configured CI checks
useCases.goal: Run pinned artifact contracts and environment-specific checks through a configured publication pipeline, inspecting failures before publication; publication is not production deployment acceptance.

useCases.name: Extract definition candidates from delivery history
useCases.goal: Derive typed Blackboard candidates from supplied pinned artifacts and journals, inspecting provenance and uncertainty before the separate client-owned draft-promotion step.

useCases.name: Maintain a governed IT definition inventory
useCases.goal: Keep typed IT definitions, their review lenses, authorizations and decision sessions coherent so every review works from the same attributable inventory.

useCases.name: Compose an IT governance fabric for an adopting scope
useCases.goal: Apply a pinned package selection to a shared subject inventory, inspect overlaps and uncovered concerns through review lenses, and retain adoption decisions against exact revisions. Composition is distinct from evaluation and enforcement.

useCases.name: Source IT definitions from inspected evidence
useCases.goal: Run revision-pinned acquisition, review its coverage limits and register the resulting candidates as drafts, keeping source revision distinct from deployed reality.

useCases.name: Run a scoped IT compliance appraisal
useCases.goal: Appraise selected definition revisions, review findings and unknown states with accountable owners, carry corrective proposals through a decision session and reappraise the revised scope. Supplied observations are needed for live-system conclusions.

useCases.name: Answer an IT question from the governed model
useCases.goal: Assess a proposed IT change by combining dependency and obligation paths with cited read-only answers over the same authorized definitions. Compare affected parties and unresolved evidence before choosing an option; graph traversal is not causal simulation.

useCases.name: Produce a named IT document family from pinned definitions
useCases.goal: Select an IT baseline and its recorded decisions, bind a versioned document family to those inputs, and review generated packs together for consistency and missing evidence. Recurring jobs preserve the same inspection and acceptance boundaries.

useCases.name: Hold definitions as the authoritative, revision-bound source
useCases.goal: Maintain typed definitions through the API and retrieve their stable identities, current revisions and retained history as one governed source. Apply tenant/object access and retention boundaries; a stored draft is not accepted intent.

useCases.name: Enforce definition lifecycle boundaries
useCases.goal: Distinguish collection closure from definition approval, validate revision-bound lifecycle changes and inspect dependent eligibility after foundation invalidation. Where the notification route is available, inform authorized consumers without conflating event delivery with approval.

useCases.name: Collect competing contributions on a shared blackboard
useCases.goal: Collect independent candidates under declared panel contracts and revisit their retained provenance to compare conflicting assertions. Contribution acceptance and evidence retention do not themselves seal a board or promote an approved definition.

useCases.name: Obtain a reproducible verdict for supplied inputs
useCases.goal: Select coherent definition revisions through the API, supply pinned inputs and Norms to evaluation, and compare verdicts across rule revisions with explicit applicability and unknown states. Repeatability applies to identical evaluation inputs, not changing live systems.

useCases.name: Run a Mechanism inside declared bounds
useCases.goal: Resolve an eligible operation and its supported adapter, apply declared authority and execution limits, then interpret the receipt against that adapter's failure contract before deciding on recovery. Wider adapters and complete execution controls require their own acceptance.

useCases.name: Serve authorized definition context to a model
useCases.goal: Provide coherent, policy-filtered definition context through a qualified API or MCP route so model requests retain revision and access boundaries. Context access alone neither grants effect authority nor validates generated answers.

useCases.name: Type a governance concern with the systemic primitives
useCases.goal: Represent a scoped governance concern using the fixed primitive roles and domain Archetypes together, exposing relationships and concerns the chosen representation cannot express. A valid representation does not establish universal model adequacy.

useCases.name: Define a domain vocabulary as an Archetype
useCases.goal: Define domain vocabulary over the fixed subject types, identify its versioned dependencies and specify how typed definitions pass through correction, review and lifecycle change. Processors implement the specified controls.

useCases.name: Express an obligation in the governance grammar
useCases.goal: Express governing intent as a Directive and evaluable Norms, and specify the review and activation boundaries of their Ascriptions. Grammar and lifecycle meaning remain distinct from runtime enforcement.

useCases.name: Adopt a sourced framework or regulation
useCases.goal: Relate selected architecture, quality and regulatory concepts to a common adopting concern, retaining clause provenance and unresolved interpretation or binding decisions. Source-content reuse does not certify legal completeness or compliance.

useCases.name: Describe an interaction with sourced protocol vocabulary
useCases.goal: Type a service, its protocol boundaries and the attribution of each assertion using selected protocol and domain vocabulary, without mistaking a schema for an adapter.

useCases.name: Take a modeling limit through research to a decision
useCases.goal: Trace a modeling limit through hypotheses, cases and recorded decisions, identify missing discriminating evidence and prepare a compatibility-aware Change Proposal where warranted. A research record is not an accepted model change or proof that an experiment ran.

useCases.name: Run an agentic workflow with deterministic controls
useCases.goal: Resolve eligible work, supply configured guidance, select a model route and correlate captured invocations for a supported local execution. Host dispatch and probabilistic generation remain distinct from deterministic workflow controls.

useCases.name: Check a produced artifact against its contract
useCases.goal: Choose the deliverable's schema and template, resolve the applicable contract and inspect violations in a mediated write set before writing. Structured validation and metadata checks do not replace substantive review or acceptance.

useCases.name: Adopt the agentic SAFe operating model
useCases.goal: Assign responsibilities from the role catalog, connect their ceremonies and handoffs, and select the practices and instructions each role needs. Qualify the harness, template and host combination separately from adopting the operating model.

useCases.name: Gate an advancement on an authenticated human decision
useCases.goal: Bind an advancement decision to the exact artifact revision and human authority, constrain the resulting work through grants and sequencing, and retain the decision trail. This gate remains planned; existing grants and journals do not authenticate approvers.

useCases.name: Deliver from a local-first, reproducible plane
useCases.goal: Produce and reconcile Git-managed artifacts using versioned deliverable contracts and captured journals, retaining evidence for review. Reproducible installation and CI publication use separately qualified routes alongside manual local setup.

useCases.name: Turn delivery history into definition candidates
useCases.goal: Correlate pinned artifact revisions with captured invocation history and derive typed candidates whose provenance, uncertainty and source limitations remain inspectable. Candidate contributions are neither accepted definitions nor evidence of deployed systems.

useCases.name: Work from shared, typed definitions
useCases.goal: Align an architect's dependency review and an AI-assisted enquiry on the same typed, versioned definition basis, tracing scope, access and interpretation differences before making a decision. A shared representation does not prove live-state correspondence or answer quality.

useCases.name: Review selected obligations together
useCases.goal: Bring source-linked frameworks, regulations and internal obligations into the same scoped review, compare overlaps and uncovered concerns, and retain accountable adoption decisions without claiming automatic conflict resolution or legal completeness.

useCases.name: Make review and activation boundaries explicit
useCases.goal: Carry a proposed governance change through explicit grammar, revision-bound review and authorized lifecycle transitions, including human decision boundaries. A research-driven model revision follows its own acceptance process; collection sealing is not activation.

useCases.name: Review candidates from selected sources
useCases.goal: Compare code-derived and delivery-derived candidates against their pinned source evidence, retain competing contributions and acquisition gaps, and select what may proceed to draft review. Confidence does not settle truth or establish deployed reality.

useCases.name: Evaluate identified inputs against supported Norms
useCases.goal: Combine reproducible Norm verdicts with scoped IT measures and findings to identify accountable corrective work and judge a subsequent appraisal. Preserve rule/input identity, applicability and unknown states; operational conclusions require observation evidence.

useCases.name: Generate artifacts through declared workflows
useCases.goal: Produce a grounded document or software artifact through assigned roles, bounded workflow execution and explicit deliverable contracts, then obtain the required revision-bound review before advancement. Technical checks, substantive acceptance and authorized deployment remain separate decisions.

values.title: Inspect acquisition scope and freshness
values.body: Distinguish inspected revisions from missing, failed or stale collection before relying on source evidence.

values.title: Align access with responsibilities
values.body: Review action-specific permissions and identity synchronization against current responsibilities, with revocation and failures explicitly verified.

values.title: Repeatable review boundaries
values.body: Reuse explicit selection and traversal rules so reviewers can compare decisions against identified subjects and snapshot boundaries.

values.title: Coherent records of related decisions
values.body: Retain agendas, participation and per-revision decisions together while keeping discussion, voting and authorized lifecycle decisions distinct.

values.title: Carry findings into corrective decisions
values.body: Connect blocking findings and uncovered obligations to owned corrections, renewed review and subsequent evidence of resolution.

values.title: Make obligation applicability explicit
values.body: Separate reusable templates and vocabulary coverage from the subjects, conditions and accountable interpretation that establish applicable obligations.

values.originalTitle: Distinguish generated output from accepted completion
values.title: Distinguish generated output from accepted completion
values.body: Inspect binding resolution, grounding constraints, missing inputs and job outcomes before accepting or reusing a generated deliverable.

values.title: Proportionate evidence preservation
values.body: Agree justified preservation periods, access and disposal constraints while keeping policy decisions distinct from verified retention enforcement.

values.originalTitle: Understand verdict changes before rule adoption
values.title: Understand verdict changes before rule adoption
values.body: Compare rule revisions on pinned reference inputs and inspect changed and unknown results before accepting their effect on decisions.

values.originalTitle: Qualify delivery hosts and model routes
values.title: Qualify delivery hosts and model routes
values.body: Evaluate host instruction delivery and model routes against explicit workload quality, cost and disclosure criteria rather than assuming interchangeable behavior.

values.title: Clear accountability for service commitments
values.body: Establish who accepts each service commitment and dependency, including responsibilities transferred to a new owner.

values.title: Time-bounded risk acceptance
values.body: Keep accepted exposure tied to accountable decisions, expiry and current compensating-control evidence rather than indefinite exceptions.

values.title: Predictable evolution of shared interfaces
values.body: Coordinate contract changes and consumer migration against explicit compatibility evidence and retirement prerequisites.

values.title: Transfer usable operational knowledge
values.body: Carry authoritative decisions, unresolved obligations and inspected evidence into a handover the receiving service owner can accept.

values.title: Remediation focused on consequential exposure
values.body: Direct security effort toward affected deployed services and business consequences, with mitigation effectiveness reviewed before closure.

values.originalTitle: Supplier decisions grounded in service exposure
values.title: Supplier decisions grounded in service exposure
values.body: Assess supplier changes and exits using dependent-service commitments, scoped assurance evidence and unresolved transition obligations.

values.title: Recovery commitments supported by evidence
values.body: Distinguish stated recovery targets from observed exercise results, dependency constraints and scenarios that remain untested.

values.title: Dependable data handoffs
values.body: Agree the meaning and quality of exchanged data with its consumers, making contract changes and conflicting requirements explicit before adoption.

values.originalTitle: Prioritize incident response by business consequences
values.title: Prioritize incident response by business consequences
values.body: Connect observed software disruption to affected business processes and accountable owners, separating confirmed impact from possible exposure so response and communication follow justified priorities.

values.title: Reduce uncertainty about a specified change
values.body: Bring relevant context and affected definitions into a shared review, making dependency paths and missing evidence visible before deciding.

values.title: Reduce time that nonconformance remains unknown
values.body: Use planned scoped evaluation to surface findings earlier, with observation coverage, freshness and unknown states visible to reviewers.

values.title: Keep consequential changes attributable
values.body: Connect consequential changes to identity, policy and revision-bound decisions as authenticated governance controls are completed.

values.title: Delegate bounded work with evidence and recourse
values.body: Build toward delegated workflows with explicit obligations, decision boundaries and controlled effects, retaining evidence for intervention and recovery.

values.title: Reduce avoidable reconstruction and rework
values.body: Reuse shared context and generated artifacts so effort can shift from repeated assembly to curation and review. Net savings depend on the workflow and compute costs.

values.title: Reduce evidence reconstruction effort
values.body: Bring linked snapshots, decisions and provenance into a stated audit scope, with completeness assessed against that review rather than inferred from history alone.

values.title: Keep governance closer to its evidence.
values.body: Bring shared definitions, reviewed candidates and scoped appraisal together to simplify reconciliation. For running systems, keep observation coverage and freshness visible.

values.originalTitle: A source of truth AI can act on.
values.title: Give AI attributable context.
values.body: Ground planned read-only answers in authorized, versioned definitions, with citations and abstention for review. Build that context through direct authoring or reviewed sourcing.

values.originalTitle: Every profile, every deliverable, one model.
values.title: Coordinate IT work around shared definitions.
values.body: Reuse common inputs across appraisal, analysis and document generation so profiles can review decisions against the same definitions. Outputs and scenarios remain subject to review.

values.title: Review obligations together.
values.body: Reuse selected packages in one scoped review, with applicability, conflicting obligations and missing evidence visible for resolution.

values.originalTitle: One place every IT profile works.
values.title: A shared workspace for IT decisions.
values.body: Author and review a common inventory through planned integrated workflows and scoped permissions, reducing handoffs between separate representations.

values.title: Make scoped appraisal inspectable.
values.body: Prepare reviews from versioned findings with visible coverage, observation age and unknown results. Legal interpretation stays with the reviewer.

values.originalTitle: Deliverables fall out of the model.
values.title: Reduce repeated document assembly.
values.body: Generate reviewable document families from reusable definitions and templates, then focus effort on review, correction and template upkeep.

values.originalTitle: See the impact before you commit.
values.title: Inspect possible effects before deciding.
values.body: Follow dependency and obligation paths to affected definitions. Timing, probability and causal predictions belong to the further simulation scope.

values.originalTitle: Ask the model, not the wiki.
values.title: Check answers against sources.
values.body: Use the planned copilot to find relevant definitions and inspect cited evidence, snapshot age and uncertainty alongside each answer.

values.title: Reduce manual candidate authoring.
values.body: Prepare proposals through staged analysis and optional inference so experts can focus on reconciliation and acceptance.

values.originalTitle: The model reflects what actually runs.
values.title: Relate definitions to inspected revisions.
values.body: Reconcile definitions against pinned source evidence. Relating them to running systems additionally requires deployed identity, configuration and fresh observations.

values.title: Inspect the basis of proposals.
values.body: Review provenance and confidence alongside retained tool details, source revisions and competing evidence.

values.title: Control sourcing data exposure.
values.body: Bound the planned sourcing workflow with explicit policies for tool/model egress, credentials, telemetry and retention, including any data leaving the local process.

values.title: Make shared context attributable.
values.body: Build toward policy-filtered snapshots that people and AI can inspect. Direct API authoring is independent of sourcing, with MCP planned as an additional interface.

values.title: Constrain operations at declared boundaries.
values.body: Combine eligibility, caller authority and adapter contracts to bound effectful execution. Keep pure verdict evaluation separate from actions that change a system.

values.title: Build toward bounded feedback loops.
values.body: Connect definitions, observations, evaluation, authorized response and re-observation in future domain-specific loops, with explicit boundaries for each integration.

values.title: Use evidence to inform revisions.
values.body: Carry reviewed candidates into authorized revisions with promotion lineage. Collection, approval and confirmation against running systems remain distinct steps.

values.title: Make transitions inspectable.
values.body: Check lifecycle advancement against defined transitions, with authentication, policy and current grammar alignment completing the governance boundary.

values.originalTitle: An API, not a document store.
values.title: Access snapshots programmatically.
values.body: Reuse structured snapshots across tools instead of manually exchanging documents, within each route's validated isolation, pagination and performance scope.

values.title: Reuse retained lifecycle evidence.
values.body: Start review from retained version history. Linking actors, rationale and retention policy completes the evidence needed for a stated audit scope.

values.originalTitle: The model announces its own changes.
values.title: React to committed changes.
values.body: Use planned change notifications to replace repeated polling, with replay and recovery for missed events.

values.title: Connect eligible definitions to bounded action.
values.body: Use defined mechanisms for named operations, adding verdicts, scheduling and feedback when building a complete domain loop.

values.title: Make pure verdicts reproducible.
values.body: Replay planned pure evaluations against pinned rules, inputs and time, independently of effectful execution.

values.originalTitle: Only the model decides what runs.
values.title: Make eligibility and authority explicit.
values.body: Bound operations through governed eligibility together with caller and adapter policy as execution controls are completed.

values.title: Identify the snapshot used.
values.body: Trace execution to requested definition IDs. Coherent pinning will distinguish latest, historical and eligible snapshot policies explicitly.

values.originalTitle: The whole picture, from every partial view.
values.title: Compare contributed partial views.
values.body: Bring conflicting candidates into shared panels so reviewers can compare evidence and identify gaps in the collected views.

values.title: Separate exploration from acceptance.
values.body: Collect candidates on the board, reconcile them in a client and govern promoted drafts in the Definition Manager through an explicit integration handoff.

values.originalTitle: You can always answer “why is this in the model?”
values.title: Trace retained proposal evidence.
values.body: Revisit captured actors and sources, with reducer decisions and Ascription links extending the trail from proposal to accepted definition.

values.originalTitle: What OpenTelemetry is to RUN, GSM is to THINK.
values.title: Build toward shared definition semantics.
values.body: Give compatible tools a common vocabulary for definitions, analogous to shared observability conventions. Interchange depends on implemented profiles and independent consumer compatibility.

values.originalTitle: Kubernetes defines infrastructure to operate it. GSM defines the world to govern it.
values.title: Make governed intent explicit.
values.body: Describe a chosen domain through typed definitions, explicit obligations and a governed lifecycle, bringing declarative intent to scoped system modeling.

values.originalTitle: Governance as code, composed with policy as code.
values.title: Connect governance and policy tools.
values.body: Use shared definitions and obligations as inputs to planned policy, attestation, observation and delivery integrations, with dedicated adapters for each tool.

values.originalTitle: Trust the standard, not the vendor.
values.title: Inspect the model and its sources.
values.body: Evaluate adoption against versioned content, source mappings and visible research questions. Neutral stewardship remains a stated direction, distinct from consortium endorsement.

values.originalTitle: Tools that interoperate, silos that fall.
values.title: Reduce bespoke semantic translation.
values.body: Reuse shared vocabulary and profiles when connecting tools that implement compatible contracts.

values.originalTitle: Lock-in ends where the standard begins.
values.title: Make portability requirements explicit.
values.body: Compare migration routes against declared conformance requirements. Complete transfer still depends on nonconformant DRAFT preservation and independent endpoint compatibility.

values.title: Adapt grammar through evidence.
values.body: Address demonstrated modeling limits through planned, reviewed extensions with explicit compatibility decisions.

values.title: Build toward neutral stewardship.
values.body: Pursue consortium stewardship through a visible model and reviewed evolution, with ownership, licensing and publication stated separately.

values.originalTitle: Day-one governance, not a blank page.
values.title: Start from reusable vocabulary.
values.body: Build on selected sourced content, then focus authoring effort on installation, interpretation and bindings for your domain.

values.originalTitle: The authority’s own taxonomy, clause by clause.
values.title: Inspect source mappings.
values.body: Review concepts in the source taxonomy with available clause references, checking coverage and legal applicability for your scope.

values.title: Review composition explicitly.
values.body: Combine selected vocabularies through GSM governance, with reference resolution and obligation conflicts handled in review.

values.originalTitle: Every claim carries where it came from.
values.title: Represent attribution explicitly.
values.body: Record attribution in typed facets and connect it to consumer-verified actors and populated lineage.

values.originalTitle: Maintained as the real world changes.
values.title: Review evolving requirements.
values.body: Use planned source monitoring and versioned updates to review changing requirements before choosing governed upgrades.

values.originalTitle: The standard is tested before it is frozen.
values.title: Challenge assumptions explicitly.
values.body: Compare alternative explanations through research records and cases, distinguishing conceptual exploration from executed testing.

values.title: Separate hypotheses from requirements.
values.body: Keep exploratory records separate from normative requirements and promote findings through specification governance.

values.title: Track open questions consistently.
values.body: Reference the same research question across cases and decisions using stable identifiers and visible status.

values.title: Build toward traceable delivery.
values.body: Generate reviewable artifacts through bounded workflows, then carry evidence forward through separate build, deployment and re-observation stages.

values.originalTitle: A method, run by agents, as a harness.
values.title: Make agentic work reviewable.
values.body: Combine role contracts, workflow decisions and artifact evidence, with planned authenticated human gates bound to exact revisions.

values.title: Coordinate through shared artifacts.
values.body: Collaborate through versioned contracts and Git-backed artifacts, reconciling separate journals, merges and version differences explicitly.

values.title: Control local delivery data.
values.body: Choose local tools and Git workflows, with explicit policies for model/tool egress, telemetry, remotes and backups.

values.title: Reuse delivery evidence.
values.body: Derive candidates from pinned artifacts and journals through the planned bridge, then review and promote them through a client-owned stage.

values.title: Inspect control decisions.
values.body: Review persisted step and write-authorization decisions within mediated execution, alongside separate checks for output quality and human approval.

values.title: Catch invalid declared artifacts earlier.
values.body: Check matched schemas before mediated writes so declared structural errors surface early. Coverage follows the supported parser, contract and transaction boundaries.

values.title: Reuse methods on supported hosts.
values.body: Carry plain-file methods between supported host/model adapters, with explicit compatibility and mediation boundaries.

values.originalTitle: An org chart, not a swarm.
values.title: Clarify responsibilities.
values.body: Assign orchestration and specialist work to named roles, making ownership and handoffs visible in each workflow.

values.title: Make expectations inspectable.
values.body: Review deliverables against shared templates, practices and workflow contracts, with executable checks supplied by supported harness bindings.

values.title: Keep decisions attributable.
values.body: Bind advancement to authenticated human decisions on exact revisions and scope through the planned approval workflow.

values.originalTitle: Your files, your history, your state.
values.title: Keep artifacts in a chosen working tree.
values.body: Own the Git working tree and its artifact history, with separate disclosure policies for journals, remotes, tools, models and backups.

values.title: Make supported setup repeatable.
values.body: Use the planned installer for pinned setup, reruns, upgrades and rollback while preserving existing work.

values.originalTitle: The same gates run in CI.
values.title: Reuse declared checks in CI.
values.body: Carry pinned artifact checks into planned CI pipelines, with environment validation and human decisions handled explicitly.

values.originalTitle: What agents actually did, made governed context.
values.title: Reuse captured delivery evidence.
values.body: Make captured delivery evidence available for review and further reasoning through planned sourcing, with missing records and uncertainty kept visible.
